title: EngramPort capability reference and grant v1, revision 3
description: Normative. A descriptor says a capability exists; a grant says a principal may use it. Neither carries a credential, a provider locator, or anything invocable. See docs/security/setup-credential-threat-model.md sections 4, 5 and 7.
$comment: WHY REVISION 3 ABANDONS PATTERN-BASED LOCATOR VALIDATION. Revisions 1 and 2 tried to tell an opaque reference apart from an opaque secret by its characters. That is impossible: `ghp_<36-char-opaque-body>` is a valid GitHub token and also a perfectly ordinary identifier, and no grammar admitting provider-chosen strings can reject it without rejecting legitimate references. Two adversarial reviews found four bypasses of successively tighter grammars, and the fifth was predicted rather than found, which is the signal that the approach was wrong. Revision 3 removes the premise: EngramPort MINTS every reference it stores. A minted reference has a shape EngramPort controls, so a provider-supplied bearer token cannot be one, not because it looks wrong but because it was never minted. Provider locators and credentials live only behind the custody boundary, keyed by the minted reference.

minted_ref.$comment: An EngramPort-minted internal reference. Format: epr:<namespace>:<uuidv7>. The namespace is closed. The UUID is generated by EngramPort at the moment the underlying provider locator or credential is placed behind the custody boundary. A provider can neither choose nor forge one: choosing requires minting, and minting requires an authorized custody write. Structural validity here does NOT imply the reference resolves; see grant_resolution_requirements.

installation_ref.$comment: Namespace-pinned. agent-a's probe of revision 3 found that a shared minted_ref let an epr:installation value sit in credential_ref and vice versa. Structurally minor, since both are minted and no provider token passes either, but a field should accept only its own namespace rather than relying on the custody resolver to notice.

capability_name.$comment: Provider-declared capability name. Untrusted display and routing text. It is never a locator, is never used to address a credential, and confers nothing.

safe_text.$comment: Bounded provider-supplied display text. Structurally unconstrained beyond length, and therefore ALWAYS subject to the recursive credential detector at ingest. This schema does not and cannot decide whether this field contains a secret.

ingest_interface.$comment: NORMATIVE PROSE, deliberately not an applicator keyword. A validator never evaluates this, and revision 2 was criticised for implying otherwise. It specifies the executable interface that threat model control A5 gates. A record passing this schema is well-formed, never trusted.
ingest_interface.entry_point: ingestCapabilityRecord(record, {tenant_id, project_id, actor_id}) -> {ok, record} | {ok: false, code}
must_fail_closed_before: any logging of the record or any field of it
any serialization to disk, wire, or cache
obligations: Recursively scan every string at any depth with the credential detector of finding F10. Reject the whole record on any hit; never strip and continue.
Reject any string parsing as a URL carrying authority: userinfo, credential-named query or fragment parameters, or a scheme outside https.
Enforce a record ceiling of 64 KiB and a maximum nesting depth of 16, so scanning cannot be exhausted.
Resolve every minted_ref against the custody store; an unresolvable, foreign-tenant, or revoked reference is refused.
Resolve shape_ref against the LOCAL shape registry only. Provider bytes may neither register nor shadow a registry entry. Registry entries are immutable and versioned; resolution pins a revision.
Fail closed on any detector, resolver, or registry error.

grant_resolution_requirements.$comment: NORMATIVE PROSE. A grant document is a CLAIM, never authority. Revision 2 permitted a forged but schema-valid grant to satisfy the documented invocation shape.
obligations: A grant document presented at invocation MUST resolve to a live server-side grant record by grant_id; the presented document is compared to the stored record and never trusted in its place.
The stored record MUST be active, unexpired against the database clock per constraint C6, and bound to the invoking tenant, project, provider, and capability.

granted_by_principal_id is NEVER accepted as proof. At grant creation the granting principal's authority is derived from the trusted resolver of threat model section 6, and the grant MUST NOT exceed or outlive it.

installation_ref and credential_ref are resolved through the custody boundary at call time, by the custody service, for the authorized consumer only. The invoking code never receives the provider locator or the credential.
A grant-shaped document with no corresponding live stored record is refused with a distinct error, and the refusal is audited.

descriptor.$comment: What a connector advertises. Attacker-influenced bytes from threat actor A6. Closed, non-invocable, and carrying NO reference of any kind: a descriptor cannot name an installation, a credential, or a minted reference, because discovery must not be able to address anything.

shape_ref.$comment: A minted reference into the LOCAL shape registry, not a provider-chosen name. A provider cannot reference a shape it did not get registered, and cannot register one.

invocable.$comment: Required and constant, so any code path treating a descriptor as invocable contradicts a field it must have read.

grant.$comment: The record of an authorization decision. Possession of this document is not authority; see grant_resolution_requirements.

granted_by_principal_id.$comment: Recorded for audit. NEVER accepted as proof of authority; the resolver supplies that at grant creation.

installation_ref.$comment: Replaces revision 2's installation_locator, which used the broad identifier grammar and accepted a JWT and a GitHub token shape. A minted reference into the custody store; the provider's real installation identifier never appears in a grant document.

credential_ref.$comment: Replaces revision 2's {manager, locator} object, whose locator accepted a GitHub token shape. The manager, the provider locator, and the credential all live behind the custody boundary, keyed by this minted reference.
